rv.q: And as our hero, Scott Folan is a bespectacled beanpole with a big future. Clever, playful and inventive, he has a terrific stage presence and carries the unpredictable score lightly. There are nicely dotty performances throughout, especially Miracle Chance as Jeremy’s inamorata Christine.
The Tony Award-nominated musical, based on the novel by Ned Vizzini is a fun, vibrant and high energy show!
For all its musical hype, this far-fetched musical can get lost in the bright lights, colours, and pulsating projections.
The show still feels a bit flabby in the middle and the story’s resolution is near-laughable, but for all the wrong reasons.
Be More Chill is a meaningful commentary on youth culture, but perhaps more importantly, it is just incredibly good fun, and that's just what we all need right now.
Bright and fun, this incredible musical feels like a combination of films like Diary of a Wimpy Kid and Scott Pilgrim Vs the World to bring a new edge to the high school comedy.
This vibrant, colourful and upbeat production is the quintessential good night out.
The entire cast of ten is excellent, selling the story with an irresistible energy that puts many larger productions to shame.
Though slightly inconsistent at times, I found myself enjoying Be More Chill much more this time around.
As it stands, it is just yet another high school musical, and not a particularly memorable one at that.

cn.t: This high-energy teen musical about a nerdy high schooler using nano-tech to become popular earns mixed-to-positive reviews. Critics praise its buzzing electronic style and Scott Folan's performance, though some find the familiar story derivative.

vr.q: it is a solid five stars from me everything i want this show to be it is doing right now
